# isFloat

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a number with a fractional part.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isFloat() — Checks whether a value is a number with a fractional part. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isFloat(value: unknown): value is number;
```

JavaScript has one numeric type, so `1.0` and `1` are the same value: the question answered is whether a fraction survives at runtime, not how the literal was written. The infinities have no fraction and are excluded.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a number with a fractional part; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `number` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isFloat(1.5); // => true
isFloat(-0.1); // => true
isFloat(42); // => false
isFloat(1.0); // => false
isFloat(Infinity); // => false
isFloat("1.5"); // => false
```
